title: fix(002): drop template docs-website spec + deploy workflow from produced apps
body:
## Problem

New project creation was fully blocked. Every scaffold failed at stagecraft's per-request `regenerateProducedIndex` fail-closed gate:

```
index is STALE ... stale shard(s): by-spec/016-docs-website (blocking diagnostics)
(scaffold job ... orphaned — operator reclaim)
```

## Root cause

#25 (`3d900fd`) stripped `website/` from produced apps but left template-encore's spec `016-docs-website`, which `establishes: ["website/", ".github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml"]`. The born-with `specs/` carry-forward drop only consulted `GENERATOR_META_SPEC_IDS` (factory-encore's own slugs, which never match a baseline slug), so every produced app carried spec 016 while `website/` was gone. The produced app's own `spec-spine index` then emitted I-004 for the missing `website/` unit and `index check` correctly failed closed. This was a genuine spec/code drift from the incomplete #25 cleanup; the stagecraft gate did its job.

## Fix

- `born-with.ts`: add `TEMPLATE_DEV_SPEC_IDS` (`016-docs-website`), consulted alongside `GENERATOR_META_SPEC_IDS` in `classifyEntry`'s `specs/` branch.
- `setup-app.ts`: drop the orphaned `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml` in the copy walk (every other workflow stays born-with the app).
- fixture + `setup-app.test.ts`: seed the spec + a kept/dropped workflow pair, with negative assertions.
- amend spec 002; regenerate the 002 registry + index shards.

## Verification

- Produced tree now passes `compile → index → index check`: **0 diagnostics, "index is fresh", exit 0** (was exit 2).
- Full adapter suite **186/186**.

title: fix(002): stop shipping the template website/ into produced apps
body:
## Problem

Every produced tenant app shipped with the template's own Docusaurus documentation site (`website/`, `baseUrl: /template-encore/`, `title: acme-vue-encore`) at its repo root. That site documents template-encore itself; it has no runtime role in a generated app.

Root cause: the born-with carry-forward classifier (`adapters/acme-vue-encore/scripts/lib/born-with.ts`) is whitelist-by-default. Any top-level entry not in a skip set falls through `classifyEntry` to the `'app'` classification and is copied into the produced app. `website/` was in no skip set, so it leaked, and nothing tested for its absence.

## Fix

- Add `'website'` to `GENERATOR_ARTIFACT_TOP_LEVEL` (the same treatment as `scripts` / `modules` / `orchestration` / `.derived`).
- Seed a `website/` entry in the synthetic baseline fixture (`makeBaselineFixture`) and add a negative assertion to `setup-app.test.ts`, so the drop is actually exercised rather than vacuously true.

## Deliberately not touched

- **`requirements/`** stays: it is the factory pipeline's **output** location (per stagecraft `importArtifacts.ts`, which deliberately excludes it from knowledge ingestion), not a leak.
- **`specs/` 000-018** stays: it is the intended born-with spec kernel that the produced app's own CI (`spec-spine index check`, coupling) needs.

## Verification

- All 19 `setup-app` carry-forward tests pass (including the new `website` assertion).
- Full local CI green: typecheck + 185 tests + lockstep (14 pinned units verified against the baseline).
- Coupling gate clean (the `scripts/` files are not spec-claimed paths).

title: fix(008): generic infra-resource compose guard + cluster-name constraint
body:
## data-redis hardening (the three review nits from #22)

Three low-severity but cheap hardening nits raised in the #22 data-redis review, closed as refinements to the FR-001 paths. No behavior change for the shipped data-redis module (`cache` matches the new regex; the guard fires identically for `redis`).

### 1. Generic compose guard (`install-module.ts`)
The `composeModule` trigger checked `manifest.infraResources.redis !== undefined` (type-specific). `infraResourcesSchema` is explicitly designed for extension (object storage, pub/sub, metrics). A future resource type added without updating this guard would parse fine and record in `template.json`, but `composeModule` would never run: a silent infra regression with no compile-time warning. Now generic: `Object.values(manifest.infraResources).some((r) => r !== undefined)`.

### 2. Cluster-name constraint (`manifest.schema.ts`)
`mergeRedis` writes `resource.cluster` as an object key reached via the `in` operator, which walks the prototype chain. An unconstrained `cluster: "__proto__"` / `"constructor"` could shadow an inherited property instead of creating an own key. `redisResourceSchema.cluster` is now `z.string().regex(/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/).default('cache')`. Manifests are adapter-authored (low blast radius), but the constraint costs nothing and closes the vector.

### 3. Shared-cluster invariant doc (`encore-composer.ts`)
`mergeRedis` is idempotent (never overwrites an existing cluster), but `removeRedis` deletes by name unconditionally. If two modules ever declared the same cluster name, decomposing either would remove the shared entry and silently break the other. Documented as an invariant so the next author picks a distinct cluster name (or makes the remove path refcounted).

### Coupling + verification
Spec 008 §5 documents the hardening (it co-owns all three FR-001 paths, so the coupling gate is satisfied by an authoring edit rather than a waiver). `spec-spine couple` 4 paths no drift, `lint` 0/0/0, `index check` fresh, composer + install-module vitest 42/42.

## Spec 009 Redis prose drift fix

The cron scheduler shipped (#20) reading the baseline `lib/redis` client over the typed `REDIS_HOST`/`REDIS_USER`/`REDIS_PASSWORD` triple (template-encore spec 018), and the data-redis promotion (#22) made that the whole contract: **there is no `REDIS_URL`**. Spec 009's prose still described the pre-promotion `REDIS_URL`/`ioredis` mechanism. This reconciles the spec to the shipped code (the `cron/manifest.json` description and `scheduler/lock.ts` were already correct).

### Prose corrections (all toward shipped reality)

- Summary, provenance, FR-003, AC-4: the lock backend is auto-detected by `isRedisConfigured()` (the typed `REDIS_HOST` connection), not `REDIS_URL`.
- FR-003 large tier: the client is the baseline `lib/redis` seam, constructed lazily so the small tier opens no socket; `ioredis` is a baseline dependency, not a cron `packageDep`.
- FR-006 `packageDeps`: drop the phantom `ioredis` entry (shipped manifest declares only `cron-parser`).
- FR-006 `envVars` / AC-6: cron declares two `SCHEDULER_*` vars, not three; the `REDIS_*` triple is baseline env owned by the data-redis resource.
- Out of scope: consumes the typed `REDIS_*` connection, not `REDIS_URL`.

### Lifecycle flip

Executes the frontmatter's staged "flips to complete on merge": `status: draft -> approved`, `implementation: in-progress -> complete`. #20 landed the module; the build-time metadata reader stays a recorded residual (does not block completion).

No code change (manifest + lock.ts already match). `spec-spine compile` 0 warnings, `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn` 0/0/0, `spec-spine index check` fresh, `spec-spine couple --base origin/main` 0 paths no drift.

title: feat(008): data-redis promotion (FR-001) - real infra.config redis resource + typed contract
body:
## What

Implements **FR-001 of spec 008**: promote `data-redis` from an inert,
falsely-labelled marker to a real, opt-in Encore `infra.config.json` `redis`
resource, reached over a fully typed connection triple.

Scoped to FR-001. FR-002 (CORS wire-or-drop) and FR-003 (dual module
composition) remain a follow-on slice, so spec 008 stays
`implementation: pending`.

## Changes

- **Manifest schema** (`manifest.schema.ts`): new `infraResources.redis`
  field so a module can declare it adds an `infra.config.json` `redis` block.
- **Composer** (`encore-composer.ts`): `mergeRedis`/`removeRedis` plus
  compose/decompose step 5 that adds and removes a topology-only `redis`
  block, mirroring the existing secrets-merge path.
- **Generate-path install** (`install-module.ts`): the guard that decides
  whether to run `composeModule` now fires for an infra-resource-only module.
  Without this, a redis-only module was recorded in `template.json` but its
  `redis` block was silently dropped on the generate path (the add/remove
  path, which calls `composeModule` directly, was unaffected).
- **data-redis manifest**: honest. It composes a `redis` block reached over
  `REDIS_HOST` / `REDIS_USER` / `REDIS_PASSWORD` (parallel to the Postgres
  `SQL_*` contract; no `REDIS_URL`). It is not a rate-limit backend (Postgres,
  INV-6) and not a session store (stateless JWT). Version 2.0.0 -> 3.0.0.
- **cron lock** (`modules/cron/...`): the large-scale lock migrates off
  `REDIS_URL` onto the typed triple via the baseline `lib/redis` client
  (template-encore spec 018). cron drops its `ioredis` dep (now baseline) and
  the `REDIS_URL` env knob. One contract, no clash.
- **Lockstep** (`baseline.lock.json`, spec 006): `pinnedRef` advanced
  `89326a5 -> ddba5e9` (template-encore main after PR #45). Hash-identical
  advance: neither invariant spec changed, both hashes re-verify byte-identical.
- **Coupling**: spec 008 promotes its FR-001 `references:` into authoritative
  `refines:` edges (001 schema + data-redis, 002 composer + install, 009 cron
  lock). Module catalog refreshed.

## Verification

- Unit + integration: 185 tests pass, including new `mergeRedis`/`removeRedis`
  and a `installModule` regression test (redis-only module composes its block).
- `spec-spine couple` OK (14 paths), `lint --fail-on-warn` clean, `index`
  fresh, `lockstep` OK (14 units against template-encore main).
- e2e structural matrix: 22/22 green.
- **End-to-end**: generated an `internal + cron + data-redis` app against
  template-encore main and ran `encore check`: the composed `infra.config.json`
  carries the typed `redis` block, cron's lock imports the baseline `lib/redis`
  client, and the app type-checks and boots.

## Follow-ups (out of scope, surfaced not fixed)

- **env-merger writes to the wrong path**: `mergeEnvVars` targets
  `<root>/.env.example` but the app's env file is `apps/api/.env.example`, so
  module env vars (both cron's `SCHEDULER_*` and data-redis's `REDIS_*`) land
  in a stray root file. Pre-existing (predates this PR; affects the merged
  cron module), so left for a dedicated fix. It does not affect the runtime
  redis contract: deployd injects `REDIS_*` at container start and the
  `infra.config.json` `redis` block is what the deploy substrate provisions
  against.
- FR-002 (CORS) and FR-003 (dual composition): the remaining spec 008 slice.

## Companions

- template-encore #45 (merged): the baseline `lib/redis` client this pins.
- OAP spec 227: surfaces Redis as an opt-in create-project resource and
  provisions it in dev via deployd `previewRedis`.

title: feat(009): tenant self-hosted cron scheduler module (OAP spec 230)
body:
## What

Adds the `cron` factory-encore module: the adapter-side realization of **OAP spec 230** (tenant self-hosted cron). Encore's `CronJob` primitive is a no-op on self-hosted deploys (there is no Encore Cloud scheduler), so this installs an in-app scheduler service into the generated Encore app, with no per-tenant Kubernetes CronJob.

Paired factory-encore spec: `009-tenant-cron-scheduler-module`.

## How it works

- **Store.** A `task_schedules` table in the base app's single `SQLDatabase("app")` (INV-11, no per-service db) via a `db/` migration, exactly as user-management adds its role tables. `register`/`list` are internal (`expose: false`) endpoints, reachable via `~encore/clients` from the app's own registration bootstrap, so no unauthenticated public surface and no auth-module dependency.
- **Polling daemon.** A `setInterval` loop selects due rows and fires each job's endpoint asynchronously, then advances `next_run_at` from the cron expression.
- **Tiered lock (the scale choice).** `tryAcquire` auto-detects `REDIS_URL`: a Postgres atomic claim by default (small scale, zero extra infra); a Redis `SET NX` lock when `REDIS_URL` is set (large scale). `ioredis` is lazily imported only on the `REDIS_URL` branch, so the small tier pulls no Redis dependency at runtime.
- **Productionized vs the prototype (spec 230 §7).** Daemon start is tied to service init (not a top-level import side-effect); firing targets `SCHEDULER_BASE_URL` with no hardcoded loopback literal in the fire path.
- **Dependencies.** `requires: [data-postgres]`, `optionalPeers: [data-redis]`. Registered in the lockstep catalog (`baseline.lock.json`) and `GENERATOR_META_SPEC_IDS` (`born-with.ts`).

## Scope / residual

- The **explicit-registration seam** ships now (FR-007). The full `encore build docker` cron-metadata **auto-extraction bridge** (FR-008) is a recorded residual: reading Encore's extracted cron metadata at runtime is version-specific and not a stable public API today.
- Out of scope: the OAP create-project form wiring (a spec-227 stage) and the `data-redis` promotion itself (spec 008). This module consumes `REDIS_URL`; it does not provision Redis.

## Validation

- `npm test`: **176 vitest** (2 new cron composition tests: compose + full round-trip decompose, INV-11 shared-db assertion).
- `spec-spine compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check` clean; `spec-spine couple --base origin/main` no drift.
- `npm run lockstep` OK (14 pinned units), with `"cron"` added to the pinned catalog.

title: docs(008): honest module surfaces: data-redis promotion, dual composition, CORS (design spec)
body:
## Summary

Design/contract spec (`008`) for the adapter-side changes the create-project reframe projects. Companion to open-agentic-platform PR #530.

Three module surfaces currently mislead, and the OAP create-project projection is only honest once they are corrected:

- **data-redis** is an inert marker (`files: {}`, `status: stable`) whose description falsely claims a Redis rate-limit backend. Promote it to a real Encore `redis` infra.config resource (a `redis` block in the generated `apps/api/infra.config.json` plus `REDIS_*` bindings), coordinated with template-encore via lockstep (spec 006). Reverses the abandoned `chore/data-redis-retirement` direction.
- **security-core**'s `CORS_ORIGIN` env knob is inert (the baseline `global_cors` is hardcoded static; nothing reads it). Decide wire-or-drop (recommended: wire it, env-aware, so deployed public/internal apps at real domains are correct).
- **dual** composes no feature modules, so a dual app cannot compose `user-management` into its internal clone. Close the gap so dual can ship staff roles.

## Coupling posture

Design-only, with one minimal in-PR code change: this spec's own meta-spec self-registration in `scripts/lib/born-with.ts` (adding `008-...` to `GENERATOR_META_SPEC_IDS` so produced apps drop it as create-time machinery). That change is claimed via an `extends: 002` additive edge, mirroring how OAP design specs add their featuregraph golden node. The remaining governed surfaces sit under `references:` and are promoted to authoritative relationships (`refines: 001`, `extends: 004`, plus template-encore baseline edits pinned via lockstep 006) by the follow-on implementation PRs.

## Validation (local parity with factory-encore CI)

- `spec-spine compile`: clean (9 specs, 0 warnings)
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: exit 0 (0 warnings)
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main`: OK, no drift (exit 0)

## Follow-ups (deferred to implementation PRs)

- The `refines: 001` (module surfaces) and `extends: 004` (dual generator) authority edges.
- The template-encore baseline edits (redis block, env-aware CORS) landed behind the lockstep pin.

## What

Retire the vestigial `data-redis` module and correct the stale "Redis is an

`REDIS_URL` knob the baseline never reads. Rate limiting has been Postgres-native

title: fix(005): the "trim built-in services" note contradicts the composition model
body:
## What

The template orchestrator's §15 "Removing Template Elements" carried a stale note (line 1747) advertising a *pending generator configuration option to trim built-in services*. This contradicts the generator's design principle.

## Why it's wrong

The generator is **compile-time composition** (spec `002-encore-generator-core`): it copies the lean `template-encore` baseline and composes modules *onto* it. It never subtracts core services. The `baseline.lock.json` split makes this explicit:

- **coreServices** (the baseline floor, unconditional): `auth`, `db`, `gateway`, `health`, `lib`, `web`
- **modules** (the additive catalog): `api-gateway`, `data-postgres`, `data-redis`, `security-core`, `user-management`

The specific target of the note, `gateway`, is a **core service**, not a module. Even the `api-gateway` module contributes `"services": []` and no Encore payload; it only adds a frontend connectivity page. The gateway is also load-bearing in the pinned `security-data-invariants` (the `89326a5` re-pin put rate limiting on the gateway), so trimming it would break a pinned invariant. A "trim built-in service" generator option is therefore incoherent, not merely unbuilt.

The legitimate **Trim phase** (Phase 5, skill `template-trim`) is untouched: it prunes only *optional composed modules and Vue views*, never core services.

## Change

- `template-orchestrator.md`: reframe the pattern from "Remove the BFF gateway" to **"Disable the BFF gateway"**. Leaving `PRIVATE_API_BASE_URL` unset makes the proxy inert without deleting the service. Drop the incoherent generator-option clause.
- `specs/005-architecture-doc-governance/spec.md` (the owning spec; coupling gate): tighten **FR-02** and **AC-2** to forbid describing the generator as offering an option to subtract, trim, or remove a core built-in service, keeping that distinct from the manual Trim phase.

## Gates (local)

- `spec-spine compile`: 8 specs, 0 warnings
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0 / 0 / 0
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main`: OK, 2 paths checked, no drift
- `npm test`: 174 passed

body:
## What and why

A coordinated ecosystem update, driven by the fact that `spec-spine` (0.10.0),
`tenant-emit`/`tenant-tail`, and the `template-encore` baseline all advanced. It
bundles the dependency bump, the coupling-gated lockstep re-pin those upstream
changes require, and the governance-hygiene gaps an audit sweep surfaced along
the way.

title: fix(born-with): carry Makefile + tools/ as governance kernel
body:
## What

The born-with carry-forward classifier (`adapters/acme-vue-encore/scripts/lib/born-with.ts`) stripped `tools/` and `Makefile` as "template-dev machinery". But the produced app's **own carried spec corpus and CI depend on both**, so every produced app was born with a red CI on its very first commit:

- Spec `000-bootstrap` (carried) declares `establishes: Makefile`. Stripping `Makefile` makes the produced app's `spec-spine index` emit a blocking `I-004` (file unit does not exist), so `spec-spine index check` fails (exit 3 / STALE).
- The carried `ci-supply-chain.yml` runs `tools/lint/workflow-pins.sh`. Stripping `tools/` makes that step exit 127 (command not found).

## Change

- Move `Makefile` and `tools/` from `GENERATOR_ARTIFACT_TOP_LEVEL` (skipped) to `BORN_WITH_KERNEL_TOP_LEVEL` (carried). They are governance substrate, not create-time machinery. The template's `tools/` today is `tools/lint/` only.
- `.derived/` stays stripped **on purpose**: it must be regenerated per produced app at scaffold time over the produced tree (carrying the template's copy would be stale and fail the produced app's own `index check`). That regeneration is a companion change on the platform scaffold; this PR just documents the intent in the code + spec.
- Update the synthetic baseline fixture (`test-helpers.ts`) and the carry tests (`setup-app.test.ts`): the "generator artifacts (skipped)" set no longer includes `tools/`/`Makefile`, and a new positive test asserts they are carried.
- Amend spec `002-encore-generator-core` FR-001 to match the canonical `born-with.ts` classifier (its Included/Excluded prose had also drifted from the kernel-carry: it listed `standards/`, `.claude/`, `specs/` as excluded though they are carried).

## Verification

Local gates green on the branch: `spec-spine compile` / `index check` (fresh) / `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0) / `couple` (no drift), `tsc --noEmit`, and the born-with unit suite (19 passed, including the new carried-substrate assertions).

Note: the `lockstep/check.test.ts` "live baseline" case (`it.runIf(source !== null)`) fails only in a local checkout that has a sibling `template-encore` clone (the live baseline has drifted from the pinned ref, a pre-existing Phase-3 pin-bump concern under spec 006). It self-skips in CI (no sibling, no `TEMPLATE_ENCORE_SOURCE`), and this PR does not touch `baseline.lock.json`, so CI is unaffected.

## Context

One of three source fixes unblocking OAP spec 220 AC-2 (produced-app CI emits a cert the spec 209 verify accepts green). Companions: `template-encore` ci.yml (`secrets: inherit` + parentless-commit routing) and the platform scaffold's per-app `.derived` regeneration. title: fix(007): make the e2e runner exit non-zero on a red combo
body:
## The bug

The CI lanes from #10 could not actually gate. `run-e2e.sh`'s `matrix()` ignored each `combo` return and terminated in `report()`, which always exited 0. So `npm run e2e:struct` / `e2e:build` returned **success even with `FAIL` rows** in the results table, making the required structural PR gate, the nightly issue-on-failure, and the drift issue-routing all **no-ops on failure**.

The first manual nightly dispatch (run 28340703409) went green, but green only meant "the script reached the end", not "22/22 built". Proven locally: a planted `FAIL` row through `run-e2e.sh report` exited `0`.

## The fix

`report()` now propagates the matrix verdict as its exit status: zero only when every recorded combo is `PASS` (or `STRUCT-OK` under `--no-build`) **and** at least one combo ran. Since `matrix` / `all` / single-`combo` all terminate in `report`, the runner now exits non-zero on any red combo (or an empty matrix). Adds spec 007 **FR-007 + AC-6** making the exit-code contract explicit.

## Verified

- planted `FAIL` row -> exit **1**; all-`PASS` -> exit **0**.
- full structural matrix **22/22 -> exit 0**.
- coupling green (2 paths), lint 0/0, index fresh.

The structural lane on this PR is now a genuine test of itself.

title: feat(007): generator e2e harness as a CI lane
body:
## What

Ports the standalone factory-encore + template-encore e2e harness into the repo as governed code under `adapters/acme-vue-encore/e2e/`, owned by new spec **`007-generator-e2e-harness`**. The harness drives the generator (spec 002) against a `template-encore` checkout across the full **22-app** profile × module matrix, replicating stagecraft's scaffold contract with **no stagecraft and no OAP** in the loop.

It closes the gap the lockstep gate (spec 006) cannot reach: lockstep pins the baseline's invariant hashes but never *compiles* the composed module payloads, so module-vs-baseline drift (an audit-API rename, a renamed `user_account` column) passes lockstep and only breaks at `encore check`. This harness builds real apps.

## Three lanes (mirroring OAP's expensive-e2e posture)

| Workflow | Trigger | What | Gating |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generator-e2e.yml` | PR, routed on the generator filter | structural matrix (`matrix --no-build`), **Node-only** (no Docker/Encore), baseline at the pinned ref | **Required** (folded into `ci-gate`) |
| `generator-e2e-nightly.yml` | cron + dispatch | full build matrix vs **pinned ref**, uploads `results.tsv`+logs, issue on failure | Non-gating |
| `generator-e2e-drift.yml` | weekly cron + dispatch | full build matrix vs **template-encore@main**, dedup'd issue-routing on divergence, fail-visible on fetch error | Non-gating |

The structural lane is Node-only because the generator skips `npm install` / `encore gen client` under `--no-install`, so it is cheap enough to gate every generator-touching PR. The expensive build matrix that catches baseline drift stays off the per-PR path. The nightly mirrors `opc-e2e-nightly`; the drift sweep mirrors `ci-factory-schema-lockstep-cron`.

## Also

- Adds `npm run e2e:struct` / `npm run e2e:build`.
- Minimal authoring edit to spec **000** FR-004 (the `ci-gate` aggregator now includes the routed structural e2e; build lanes are scheduled + non-gating) so the kernel's description of its own CI surface stays accurate.
- Updates README + CLAUDE.md (editorially governed); refreshes the registry + index shards.

## Verification

- Structural matrix **22/22 green** locally.
- typecheck clean, lint 0/0, index fresh, coupling gate green (12 paths, no drift).

title: chore(governance): prune three loose ends (compile cache, lockstep pin, package description)
body:
A repo audit (clean gates, all spec-claimed paths present, no old-name leakage) surfaced three independent loose ends. Each is addressed below, one by one. No behavioral change to the generator.

## 1. Untrack the non-deterministic compile cache
`.derived/spec-registry/build-meta.json` embeds a wall-clock `builtAt`, so it is not byte-deterministic (constitution Principle 2) and dirtied the working tree on **every** `compile`/`/init`. The last commit on `main` carried exactly this timestamp churn. This PR `git rm --cached`s it and adds a `.gitignore` rule. The deterministic registry shards stay tracked; the codebase-index hash (`spec-spine index check`) remains the real staleness gate, so nothing is lost.

## 2. Refresh the cross-repo lockstep pin (b37d3d7 → c7603ee)
The pin lagged `template-encore` main by two merged commits. I verified the intervening main commits touch **no pinned unit**:
- 001/002 invariant `spec.md` hashes re-hash **identical** at `c7603ee` (`1a70230a…`, `487f6ec8…`).
- The six baseline core services are unchanged.
- Dimension 3 (module catalog) checks factory-encore's own catalog, not the baseline.

So the bump moves only the ref, not the enforced content. Recorded in `baseline.lock.json` and `specs/031` FR-003, which already declares a ref bump "a deliberate, coupling-gated edit to this spec." Coupling gate: OK, 3 paths, no drift.

> Note (not changed here): local `npm run lockstep` resolves `--source` to the sibling `template-encore` checkout, so it validates against whatever branch that checkout is on, while CI fetches the pinned ref. Worth keeping in mind; left as-is by design (FR-005 local verifiability).

## 3. Fix the package.json description
The gates governing this repo's code are the **spec-spine kernel + cross-repo lockstep**, not the OAP runtime `FAC-S*` validation stages (which the adapter's orchestration prose references as an external factory-runtime concern). Wording corrected.

## Gates (local)
- `vitest`: 167 passed (11 files)
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0/0/0
- `spec-spine index check`: fresh
- `npm run lockstep`: OK against the new pin (`c7603ee`)
- `spec-spine couple --base main`: OK, 3 paths, no drift

title: docs: scrub em dashes from .claude surface, fix bootstrap example
body:
## What

Two house-style cleanups on the inherited Claude Code surface (merged in #3), bundled per the follow-up note:

1. **Em-dash scrub.** House style forbids U+2014. The 13 agent/skill/rule files carried **137** em dashes; every one is replaced with a colon, semicolon, or comma chosen by context:
   - Glossary-style `**label** — description` list items → `**label**: description` (the dominant pattern).
   - Conjunction continuations (` — or before…`) → comma.
   - Spots where a colon would collide with an existing colon on the line (e.g. `Compliance: [… deviates: …]`, `{ran / skipped: reason}`, the `make X: cmd: description` nested list) → comma or semicolon instead, to avoid awkward double colons.

2. **Bootstrap example fix.** `.claude/rules/governed-artifact-reads.md` showed `npx spec-spine registry show 000-bootstrap --json` in its "Good pattern" block. There is no `000-bootstrap` id, so the example would error if run. Repointed at the real first spec, `000-factory-kernel`.

## Why it's safe

- `.claude/**` is **not** hashed by the codebase index (`spec-spine.toml` hashes only `standards/**` and `.github/workflows/**` beyond the always-hashed core), so this trips neither the staleness gate nor the coupling gate.
- Verified locally: `spec-spine index check` → fresh; `spec-spine couple --base origin/main` → 0 paths, no drift; `registry show 000-factory-kernel` resolves.
- Diff is balanced (137 insertions / 137 deletions); content unchanged apart from punctuation and the one corrected id.

title: feat: factory generator home (Phase 1) + lockstep invariant pin activation (Phase 3)
body:
## Factory restructure: generator home (Phase 1) + lockstep invariant pin (Phase 3)

This PR bundles the two factory-side phases as one unit (deliberately not landed direct to `main`). **Phase 1** makes factory-encore the create-time generator home; **Phase 3** activates the cross-repo lockstep invariant pin now that template-encore's baseline is finalized at `b37d3d7`.

Implements the OAP create-time vs runtime split. factory-encore now owns everything create-time; template-encore (public identity `acme-vue-encore`) keeps only the runnable product (Phase 2, separate session).

### What landed (Phase 1)

**Kernel + CI** (spec `000-factory-kernel`). factory-encore now carries governed code, so it earns a kernel: `package.json` (tsx + vitest, `spec-spine` 0.8.0 pinned), `spec-spine.toml`, `standards/`, and a resilient CI surface. The terminal `ci-gate` aggregates the governance gate (`spec-spine.yml`: compile + `lint --fail-on-warn` + index-staleness + PR coupling), the generator tests (`generator-ci.yml`), the lockstep (`ci-lockstep.yml`), and an AI PR review (`ai-pr-review.yml`) that **passes with a visible PR notice on a Claude API outage** and hard-fails only on auth errors.

**Generator** (specs `007`-`010`). `scripts/` + `modules/` moved into `adapters/acme-vue-encore/`. The generator is source-parameterized (`--source <template-encore checkout>`, it no longer assumes it lives in the app tree) and materializes as **"lean baseline + compose"** rather than copy-superset-and-trim.

**Born-with output policy** (`scripts/lib/born-with.ts`). Replaces the retired product-side `EXCLUDED_TOP_LEVEL`. A produced app is born with the governance kernel (`standards/`, `spec-spine.toml`, `.claude/`, `CODEMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`) plus the app and app-invariant specs, and carries none of the generator, the module catalog, or the generator meta-specs.

**Identity.** `adapter.name: encore-vue -> acme-vue-encore`; dir renamed via `git mv`; docs updated.

**Lockstep** (spec `031-factory-schema-lockstep`). A tsx/vitest cross-repo check binds the generator + module catalog to the template-encore baseline. The mechanism is fully wired (structure + catalog binding enforced); in Phase 1 the **001/002 invariant-hash pin was DEFERRED to the Phase 3 handshake** (001 changes in Phase 2 when it absorbs the static-serving wiring from spec 010). The deferral was a visible notice, never a silent skip. That handshake is now part of this PR (below).

### What landed (Phase 3 handshake: lockstep pin activation)

template-encore main is finalized at `b37d3d7`, so the deferred 001/002 invariant-hash pin is now **active** (commit `fdd4cbf`):

- `invariantPin.status`: `deferred` -> `pinned`; `hashes` filled with the **SHA-256 of each spec.md** at the pinned ref (`001` = `1a70230a...`, `002` = `487f6ec8...`). The git blob SHA-1 shorthands `4235fd3f`/`4596af31` name the same blobs but are NOT the stored value: `check.ts` compares the content SHA-256 by exact string, so storing the blob hash would have produced a permanent DRIFT failure.
- `pinnedRef`: `e57f7e5` -> `b37d3d7`.
- **Dimension 3 adapted.** Phase 2 stripped the `modules/` catalog out of the baseline, so `verifyCatalogBinding` now checks factory-encore's catalog only; the obsolete baseline-side assertion is dropped. (The invariant pin itself needed no checker change, per AC-4; the catalog dimension did, because the baseline it once mirrored no longer exists.)
- Tracked through the owning spec `031` (summary, FR-001/002/003, AC-1/2/4) and the refreshed derived registry + index, so the coupling gate stays green.

### Green locally

```
typecheck: PASS    vitest: 167 passed    npm run lockstep: PASS (pin active, 13 units, no DRIFT)
spec-spine: compile 0 warnings | lint --fail-on-warn 0 | index fresh
```

### Coordination (Phase 2 / Phase 3)

- **Phase 2** (template-encore): done. The generator copy + module catalog were stripped to a lean `acme-vue-encore` reference app, merged to main at `b37d3d7` (no leftover generator surface).
- **Phase 3** (handshake): done in this PR. 001/002 hashes pinned and the lockstep hash dimension is green.
- Two cuts flagged for template sign-off rather than resolved unilaterally: the spec-010 FR-003 static-serving cut (contract relocating into product spec 005) and the exact `validate` split (FAC-S* boundary half here vs born-with checks 0..15 in the product).
